correctness.rationale: For fixed b, \(tb^t/(1-b^t)\) strictly decreases in t, so \(\rho_t\) strictly increases and tends to \((1+b)/(1-b)\), proving the exact no-activation boundary b<=3/5. Since \(\rho_t<t\), activation cannot precede step five. Algebra gives \(\rho_t>4\) iff \(F_t(b)>0\), with \(F_t=(b-1)^2P_t\). The coefficients of \(P_t\) have exactly one sign change; \(P_t(3/5)<0<P_t(1)\), so Descartes plus continuity gives one positive root in the required interval. Monotonicity of \(\rho_t\) orders the roots. The exact root identity for \(\delta_t=b_t-3/5\) implies exponential smallness and then \(\delta_t\sim(4/25)t(3/5)^t\). A fresh independent numerical replay reproduced b_5 through b_11 and the stated activation indices for 0.8, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, 0.7, 0.65, and 0.61.
residual_risks: The theorem applies to the original strict \(\rho_t>4\) gate; implementations using a different gate need a different sequence.

final_claim: For the source RAdam gate \(\rho_t>4\), rectification never activates exactly for \(0<\beta_2\le3/5\); for each \(t\ge5\) there is a unique root \(b_t\in(3/5,1)\) of \(P_t(b)=-3-b+\sum_{j=2}^{t-1}(2j-3)b^j\), the roots decrease to \(3/5\), and the first rectified step is exactly t iff \(b_t<\beta_2\le b_{t-1}\). Moreover \(b_t-3/5\sim(4/25)t(3/5)^t\).
